About us

We pride ourselves on the knowledge that we are part of a story of Pacific people in Aotearoa New Zealand that goes back many hundreds of years, and reaches across many thousands of miles. Our job is to write the next chapter of this story for our people. We see our connection to the Pacific community, therefore, as being at the intersection between centuries of history and culture, and the future Aotearoa New Zealand. In everything we do, we take our families and communities with us. Whenever we are in meetings with other Agencies, designing policy or speaking with Ministers of Parliament, we take our communities into the room with us. We can do this because of the time we spend nurturing our relationships with our people. These relationships are crucial to what we do and enable us to prioritise the changes that will ensure more of our Pacific people can lead fulfilling lives. Whether it is accessing life changing learning opportunities, help finding jobs to support their families, or having their voice heard in government decisions that affect Pacific communities, we walk alongside our people and empower them to change their lives.

    "For me, it's about being proud of your identity and your heritage. It's important that our people here in Aotearoa continue to hold on to our language."  ❤️ For decades, Okesene Faraimo has dedicated himself to preserving and promoting Te Gagana Tokelau (Tokelau language), helping ensure future generations can stay connected to their language, culture and identity. In recognition of his services to Te Gagana Tokelau and culture, Okesene has been appointed a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit. His contributions have been wide-ranging, from serving on language steering groups and the National Tokelau Aotearoa Leaders Council to helping shape the Ministry for Pacific Peoples' Pacific Languages Strategy 2022–2032, ensuring Tokelau voices were represented and heard. Read more about his inspiring journey: https://bit.ly/4vbBHAL

    From classrooms to the stage, Fane Fusipongi Ketu’u has dedicated decades to championing Lea Faka-Tonga – the Tongan language ❤️ Her commitment is now being recognised with her appointment as a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit for services to Tongan language. “My hope and prayers are that this honour will inspire others to continue championing our Pacific Languages and cultures. Our young people deserve to know that their language is a gift, a source of strength, and something to treasure with pride.” says Fane. “Every time we teach and learn our language, speak it with pride, and make sure we pass it on to the next generation, it strengthens who we are as Tongan people.” “I have been given this honour, but this is one for the Tongan community." Read more about Fane’s dedication to Lea Faka-Tonga: https://bit.ly/4w6ocD8

    The Ministry for Pacific Peoples was honoured to attend and celebrate the Tongan Society South Canterbury’s 10-year anniversary, held on 30 May in Timaru. 🇹🇴 The Timaru Deputy Mayor Scott Shannon, along with other distinguished guests, joined the community to mark the occasion. The Tongan Society South Canterbury started from humble beginnings, with a few families gathering with limited resources but a shared vision. Over time, it has grown into a strong and vibrant community network, supporting and uplifting families across the region. It was a fitting tribute to a community that may be small, but is mighty in spirit, resilience, and capability. This milestone celebration not only recognised ten years of the society’s journey but also highlighted the many achievements and contributions of the Tongan community in South Canterbury.

    New Zealand Football has been recognised with a national award at the Sport New Zealand Ihi Aotearoa and Recreation Awards in Tāmaki Makaurau.🏅 The Leadership in Diversity and Inclusion Award recognises a three-year partnership between the Ministry for Pacific Peoples and New Zealand Football to grow Pacific participation in football and create more opportunities for Pacific communities to connect with the game, on and off the field. Through initiatives like football festivals and talanoa workshops, Pacific communities across Aotearoa are getting more involved in the sport. Congratulations to New Zealand Football on this well-deserved recognition and your ongoing commitment to Pacific communities. 👏 Read more at the link below. 👇 https://lnkd.in/eQ7qGRqS

    The Ministry for Pacific Peoples attended the 125th anniversary celebration of Niue as part of the Realm of New Zealand, hosted by the Niue diaspora community and held in Ōtautahi Christchurch on Saturday. Her Excellency the Rt Hon Dame Cindy Kiro, Niue Government Minister Hon Richie Mautama, and other distinguished guests joined the community in marking the occasion. From the first families who settled in Christchurch, the Niue community has built a legacy of resilience, unity, and pride, sustained through language, faith, and community. Fakaaue lahi to our Christchurch Niue community for honouring the past and inspiring the future for our communities.

    A significant milestone for women across the public sector. Recently, our Secretary for Pacific Peoples, Gerardine Clifford-Lidstone, attended the launch of the Government Women's Network | Te Aka Wāhine o Aotearoa Strategy 2026–2029. As a new co-sponsor of the network, it was a valuable opportunity to celebrate this important milestone in strengthening leadership, equity and connection for women across the public sector. The strategy aims to strengthen connections, amplify the voices of women, and support women to participate, progress and lead. We look forward to supporting the Government Women's Network and its continued impact across the sector.
